Authority.
This part is issued under the authority of sections 103, 201, 202, and 310 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (
43 U.S.C. 1702
,
1711-1712
,
1740
).
§ 1601.40
Environmental compliance.
The Bureau of Land Management will comply with the National Environmental Policy Act for the proposed plan, revision, or amendment as part of the land use planning process and, wherever possible, the proposed plan, revision, or amendment and related environmental compliance shall be published in a single document.
§ 1601.50
Scope.
(a) This part applies to all public lands subject to section 202 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act.
(b) This part also governs the development, revision, amendment, or maintenance of land use plans when the only public land interest is the mineral estate.
§ 1601.60
Principles.
The development, revision, and amendment of land use plans will provide for public involvement and, unless otherwise provided by law, shall be consistent with the principles of multiple use and sustained yield described in sections 103 and 202 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976.
§ 1601.70
Administrative remedy.
A decision issued pursuant to the procedures in this Part is the final decision for the Department of the Interior and is not reviewable by the Office of Hearings and Appeals.
Subpart 1610—Land Use Planning
§ 1610.10
Land use plans.
(a) Land use plans are described by the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 and document the Bureau of Land Management's decisions for the use of public lands. A decision to approve the development, revision, or amendment of a land use plan guides and controls future management actions and does not generally authorize any uses of the public lands, which are usually approved through project-specific implementation decisions. A land use plan, in contrast, establishes a framework for the Bureau of Land Management to consider proposed uses of public lands, and consists of:
(1) Desired resource use and condition objectives;
(2) Designations identified by statute, regulation, or national policy of land areas for exclusive purposes or uses;
(3) Lands allocated for allowable resource uses; and
(4) Management direction for the general management practices or program constraints needed to achieve the resource use and condition objectives.
(b) The Bureau of Land Management will establish intervals and standards for monitoring and evaluating the plan to determine the effectiveness of the plan and the need for amendment or revision.
(c) State Directors will provide quality control and supervisory review, including plan approval, for the development, revision, and amendment of plans and related environmental review.
(d) The Bureau of Land Management refers to land use plans as resource management plans.
§ 1610.20
Public participation.
(a) The public shall be provided opportunities to meaningfully participate in and comment on the development, revision, and amendment of plans. Opportunity for public participation in land use planning shall be appropriate for the areas and people involved. Opportunities for public participation shall at a minimum be provided at the following specific points in the planning process:
(1) General notice at the outset of the process consistent with § 1610.42; and
(2) Publication of the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment, which triggers the opportunity for protest consistent with § 1610.51.
(b)(1) Any public comment period provided will be 30 calendar days beginning the day after the notice. The Bureau of Land Management may extend a public comment period for a period not to exceed an additional 30 calendar days.
(2) The Bureau of Land Management may offer a public meeting or hearing in lieu of providing a public comment period identified at paragraph (b)(1) of this section when adequate notice is provided, except when a comment period is required by the National Environmental Policy Act.
(c) Public opportunity to protest on the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment pursuant to § 1610.51 will be 30 calendar days beginning the day after the publication of the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment and cannot be extended.
§ 1610.30
Coordination with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, and Indian tribes.
The following sections outline the coordination and consistency procedures for land use planning.
§ 1610.31
Coordination of planning efforts.
(a) In addition to the public involvement prescribed by § 1610.20, the Bureau of Land Management will coordinate with other Federal agencies, state and local governments, and federally recognized Indian tribes consistent with section 202(c)(9) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act.
(1) Coordination during the land use planning process means inviting the participation of Federal agencies, State and local governments, and Indian tribes germane to the planning area in the development, revision, or amendment of a land use plan to advise on the general approach of the planning effort as representatives of people and institutions that are affected by decisions made in land use plans.
(2) [Reserved]
(b) When developing, revising, or amending land use plans, State Directors shall consider approved resource-related plans in the land resource management programs of State, local, and federally recognized Tribal governments submitted by these entities in the land use planning coordination process.
(1) Approved resource-related plans means plans and policies for resource management programs germane to the development of land use plans for public lands prepared and approved pursuant to and in accordance with authorization provided by State, local, or Tribal constitutions, legislation, or charters for the relevant governmental entity.
(2) [Reserved]
(c) State Directors shall, to the extent practicable, keep apprised of approved State and local governmental and Indian tribal plans that are germane in the development of land use plans for public lands, but they shall not be accountable for considering plans if they have not been provided to the Bureau of Land Management in a timely manner by State and local governments or Indian tribes.
§ 1610.32
Seeking consistency with State and local plans.
(a) The development, revision, or amendment of a land use plan shall be consistent to the maximum extent consistent with Federal law and the purposes of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act with approved
(
printed page 72508)
resource-related plans of State and local governments, so long as these plans are consistent with the purposes, policies, and programs of Federal laws and regulations applicable to public lands.
(1) Consistent means that, as a general rule, no use of public land should be permitted which is prohibited by approved resource-related plans of State or local governments that are germane to the development of land use plans for public lands, unless such use is found by the Bureau of Land Management to be in the national interest.
(2) Approved resource-related plans means plans and policies for resource management programs germane to the development of land use plans for public lands prepared and approved pursuant to and in accordance with authorization provided by State or local constitutions, legislation, or charters for the relevant governmental entity.
(b) State Directors shall not be accountable for ensuring consistency if they have not been notified in a timely manner, in writing, by State and local governments of an apparent, specific inconsistency.
§ 1610.40
Land use planning process.
The following sections outline procedures for conducting the land use planning process.
§ 1610.41
Preparing for planning.
(a) In preparing for planning, the Bureau of Land Management will:
(1) Assemble existing resource, environmental, social, economic, and institutional data and information. Inventory data and information shall be assembled in a manner that aids application in the planning process, including subsequent monitoring requirements.
(2) Request approved resource-related plans of State and local governments and Indian tribes. The Bureau of Land Management will ask State and local governments and Indian tribes to identify plans they have approved that are germane to the Bureau of Land Management's development of land use plans, as well as a summary of the uses that each such government plan generally prohibits or restricts. State and local governments and Indian tribes have 45 calendar days to provide the requested information for it to be considered by the Bureau of Land Management.
(3) For the development or revision of a land use plan, document a profile of the planning area and analysis framework to inform the planning process. This will include the current conditions, trends, and forecasts for resources, resource uses, existing designated uses of public lands, and social and economic conditions within the planning area. The Bureau of Land Management will provide a framework for the analysis to avoid unnecessary data collection and analysis and will present the preliminary alternatives under consideration for the planning effort. The State Director will make this document publicly available.
(b) [Reserved]
§ 1610.42
Public notice of planning.
The State Director will provide public notice when the Bureau of Land Management initiates the development, revision, or amendment of a land use plan and will request public participation consistent with § 1610.20(a) and (b).
§ 1610.43
Proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment.
Prior to approving a land use plan, revision, or amendment, the State Director will publish a proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment, which will be subject to public protest pursuant to § 1610.51. The proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment shall establish intervals and standards, as appropriate, for monitoring and evaluation of the plan.
§ 1610.50
Land use plan pre-decisional review, approval, use, and modification.
The following sections describe the procedures for pre-decisional review, approval, use, and modification of approved land use plans.
§ 1610.51
Protest procedures.
(a) Any person who participated in the planning process and has an interest which is or may be adversely affected by the approval of a land use plan, revision, or amendment may protest such proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment. A protest may raise only those issues submitted to the Bureau of Land Management during the planning process or issues concerning substantial changes to a proposed plan, revision, or amendment made by the State Director and that could not previously have been raised during the planning process.
(1) Any protest shall be in writing and filed electronically with the Bureau of Land Management Headquarters through the agency's national register for National Environmental Policy Act related documents. Consistent with § 1610.20(c), any protest must be received within 30 calendar days following the publication of the proposed plan, revision, or amendment on the agency's national register for National Environmental Policy Act related documents.
(2) The protest shall contain:
(i) The name and interest of the person filing the protest;
(ii) A statement of the issue or issues being protested; and
(iii) A concise statement explaining why the State Director's proposed decision is believed to be inconsistent with relevant law, regulation, or policy.
(3) The Office of the Bureau of Land Management Director shall render a decision on each protest before the Bureau of Land Management approves a plan, revision, or amendment.
(b) The Office of the Bureau of Land Management Director will publish written responses to any protests it received, setting forth the reasons for the Bureau of Land Management Director's resolution of the protest.
§ 1610.52
Governor's consistency review procedures.
(a) Prior to the public release of a proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment, the State Director shall submit to the Governor of the State involved, the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment and shall identify known inconsistencies with approved State plans.
(b) The Governor shall have 30 calendar days beginning the day after receipt of the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment to identify additional inconsistencies and provide recommendations for resolving inconsistencies in writing to the State Director. Recommendations from the Governor must be received within 30 calendar days to be considered by the Bureau of Land Management. If the Governor does not provide a recommendation to resolve inconsistencies, they are presumed resolved.
§ 1610.53
Local governments' consistency review procedures.
(a) Prior to the public release of a proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment, the State Director shall submit to the appropriate officials for the local governments within the planning area, the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment and shall identify known inconsistencies with approved local plans.
(b) The local government official shall have 30 calendar days beginning the day after receipt of the proposed land use plan, revision, or amendment to identify additional inconsistencies and provide recommendations for resolving inconsistencies in writing to the State Director. Recommendations from the local government official must be received within 30 calendar days to be considered by the Bureau of Land Management. If the local government
(
printed page 72509)
official does not provide a recommendation to resolve inconsistencies, they are presumed resolved.
§ 1610.54
Land use plan approval.
(a) Following the resolution of any protest under § 1610.51, and the resolution of any inconsistencies identified by the Governor under § 1610.52 or local government officials under § 1610.53, the State Director will issue a decision concerning the approval of the plan, revision, or amendment.
(b) The Bureau of Land Management's decision concerning the approval of a plan, revision, or amendment under paragraph (a) of this section is the final decision of the Department of the Interior.
§ 1610.55
Conformity and implementation.
(a) All future authorizations and actions shall conform to the Bureau of Land Management's approved plan. Conformance means that the use, authorization, or action is provided for by the land use plan or, if not provided for, shall be consistent with the decisions of the approved land use plan, unless specifically authorized otherwise by law.
(b) If a proposed action is not in conformance and warrants further consideration before a plan revision is scheduled, such consideration shall be through a plan amendment in accordance with the provisions of § 1610.57.
(c) The Bureau of Land Management shall be responsible for monitoring and evaluating its approved land use plans in accordance with the established intervals and standards and at other times as appropriate to determine whether there is sufficient cause to warrant amendment or revision of the plan based on new data, new or revised policy, or a change in circumstances.
§ 1610.56
Maintenance.
(a) In circumstances when the President or Congress establishes land uses or restrictions of land uses on public lands either through proclamation or law, the Bureau of Land Management will document maintenance to update applicable land use plans to reflect the decision of the higher-level authority. Any other changes to established land use planning decisions other than those expressly made by the proclamation or law must be reviewed through planning procedures for amendment or revision pursuant to §§ 1610.57 and 1610.58.
(b) The Bureau of Land Management may document maintenance to correct errors and is limited to further refining the documentation of a decision of the approved plan. Maintenance shall not result in expansion in the scope of resource uses or restrictions, or change the decisions of the approved plan.
(c) Maintenance is not considered a plan amendment and shall not require the formal public involvement and interagency coordination process described under §§ 1610.20 and 1610.30 or environmental review.
(d) Maintenance shall be documented in plans and supporting records.
§ 1610.57
Amendment.
A land use plan may be changed through amendment to maintain decisions providing for the management of public lands that are current. An amendment shall be initiated, as appropriate, by the Bureau of Land Management's consideration of monitoring and evaluation findings (§ 1610.55(c)) or a proposed action that would result in a change in the scope of resource uses or a change in a limited scope of the decisions of the approved plan. If the amendment is being considered in response to a specific proposal, the analysis required for the proposal and for the amendment may occur simultaneously and in the same documentation.
§ 1610.58
Revision.
A land use plan shall be revised when the Bureau of Land Management contemplates substantial changes to the scope of the planning decisions providing for the management of public lands. A revision shall be initiated, as appropriate, based on the Bureau of Land Management's consideration of monitoring and evaluation findings (§ 1610.55(c)) affecting the entire plan or major portions of the plan.
§ 1610.60
Management decision review by Congress.
Any Bureau of Land Management planning decision that totally eliminates one or more principal or major uses listed at section 103(l) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act for two or more years with respect to contiguous tracts of 100,000 acres or more, shall be reported to Congress. This report shall not be required prior to approval of a land use plan which, if fully or partially implemented, would result in such an elimination. The required report shall be submitted as the first action step in implementing that portion of a land use plan which would require elimination of such a use.
§ 1610.70
Designation of areas of critical environmental concern.
(a) The Bureau of Land Management shall identify and evaluate if public lands have the potential for areas of critical environmental concern designation and management for protection against irreparable damage. The Bureau of Land Management evaluates and considers designation only through the process of developing or revising a land use plan, or when amending a land use plan when the evaluation and consideration falls within the scope of the amendment. If a nomination for an area of critical environmental concern is received outside of the planning process, the evaluation and consideration will be deferred to an upcoming planning process.
(b) In order for the Bureau of Land Management to designate an area of critical environmental concern, it must find that an area of public lands meets all three of the following criteria:
(1)
Relevance.
There shall be present historic, cultural, or scenic values, fish and wildlife resources or other natural systems or processes, or natural hazards.
(2)
Importance.
The resource, system, process, or hazard that the Bureau of Land Management determines to be relevant shall also have substantial value. This generally requires characteristics that demonstrate qualities of more than localized distinctiveness, especially when compared to similar resources. A natural hazard can be important if it is a threat to human life or property.
(3)
Special management attention.
The area requires special management to protect and prevent irreparable damage from a reasonably foreseeable use to those values that the Bureau of Land Management determines to be relevant and important.
(c) The boundaries of designated areas of critical environmental concern shall encompass the smallest area of public lands necessary to protect and prevent irreparable damage of the relevant and important values.
(d) The State Director, through the land use planning process, may in whole or in part remove or modify the designation of an area of critical environmental concern.
§ 1610.80
Transition period.
(a) Proposed management actions must conform to approved management framework plans until such time as those plans are superseded by land use plans or amended under § 1610.57.
(b) The Bureau of Land Management is not required to initiate land use planning in areas with no land use plan
(
printed page 72510)
or a management framework plan, except to consider the sale of lands consistent with section 203 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act. The Bureau of Land Management will consider proposed actions on unplanned public lands consistent with applicable Federal statutes and procedures.
Subpart 1611—Amending Land Use Plans To Address Emergencies
§ 1611.10
Emergency procedures.
(a) To address emergency circumstances, any individual in the Office of the Secretary who has been appointed by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate, may, consistent with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act and other applicable law, authorize modified procedural requirements that depart from those otherwise required by this subpart for amending land use plans, to facilitate review of a proposed implementation action to address the emergency circumstances. Modified procedures may include:
(1) Public participation. Reducing the timeframes required for public participation described at § 1610.20(b) or (c), or waiving the requirement for public participation at notice described at § 1610.20(a)(1) or protest described at § 1610.20(a)(2), but not waiving both.
(2) Coordination. Waiving the specific procedures for invitation to participate in coordination described at § 1610.31(a) and the review of plans for consideration described at § 1610.31(b). If these procedures are waived, communications tailored to collect only the information needed to support the plan amendment under review must occur.
(3) Consistency. Reducing the timeframes required to respond to the Bureau of Land Management's request for approved resource-related plans of State and local governments and Indian tribes and statement of prohibited uses described at § 1610.41(a)(2) and for the Governor's consistency review described at § 1610.52(b) and local governments' consistency review described at § 1610.53(b), or waiving the requirement to request plans or hold consistency reviews for the Governor and local governments, but not waiving both.
(b) The authority to apply emergency procedures of paragraph (a) of this section applies only for the duration of emergency circumstances and only for the preparation of land use amendments supporting the review of a project(s) that respond to the emergency circumstances.
(c) At the start of the planning effort, the State Director will publish the modified planning procedures to inform the public and other Federal agencies, State and local governments, and Indian tribes how the requirements for public involvement, coordination, and consistency during planning on public lands will be met for the amendment.

ACTION:
Notice of proposed rulemaking and notice of public hearing; correction.
SUMMARY:
This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the
Federal Register
on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
DATES:
The deadline for submitting written or electronic comments on the proposed rule was October 26, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Commenters are strongly encouraged to submit public comments electronically. Submit electronic submissions via the Federal eRulemaking Portal at
https://www.regulations.gov
(indicate IRS and REG-116506-25) by following the online instructions for submitting comments. The public hearing will be conducted by telephone only. Once submitted to the Federal eRulemaking Portal, comments cannot be edited or withdrawn. The Department of the Treasury (Treasury Department) and the IRS will publish any comments submitted electronically or on paper to the public docket. Send paper submissions to: CC:PA:01:PR (REG-116506-25), Room 5503, Internal Revenue Service, P.O. Box 7604, Ben Franklin Station, Washington, DC 20044.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Concerning the proposed regulations under section 1400Z-2, Dominic DiMattia of the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Income Tax and Accounting) at (202) 317-7009 (not a toll-free number); concerning the remainder of the proposed regulations under sections 6011, 6037, 6039K, 6039L, 6045, 6722, 6724, and 6726, Roseann Cutrone of the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Procedure and Administration) at (202) 317-6844 (not a toll-free number); and concerning submissions of comments or the public hearing, the Publications and Regulations Section at (202) 317-6901 (not a toll-free number) or by sending an email to
publichearings@irs.gov
(preferred).

AGENCY:
Federal Emergency Management Agency, Department of Homeland Security.
ACTION:
30-Day notice of extension and request for comments.
SUMMARY:
The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) will submit the information collection abstracted below to the Office of Management and Budget for review and clearance in accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. FEMA invites the general public to take this opportunity to comment on an extension of a currently approved information collection. In accordance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, this notice seeks comments concerning the After Action Report/Improvement Plans, Integrated Preparedness Plans, and Support Request Forms to the National Exercise Program which are used to validate current preparedness capabilities and support future national exercise efforts.
DATES:
Comments must be submitted on or before December 10, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Written comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection should be sent within 30 days of publication of this notice to
www.reginfo.gov/​public/​do/​PRAMain
.
Find this particular information collection by selecting “Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments” or by using the search function.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Requests for additional information or copies of the information collection should be made to Director, Information Management Division, 500 C Street SW, Washington, DC 20472, email address
FEMA-Information-Collections-Management@fema.dhs.gov
or Sayoko Hamilton, Section Chief, Performance Analysis and Evaluation, Resilience, FEMA at 202-674-3803, or
Sayoko.Hamilton@fema.dhs.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Presidential Policy Directive 8 (PPD-8: National Preparedness), issued on March 30, 2011, establishes a National Preparedness Goal (NPG) that identifies the core capabilities necessary for preparedness and a National Preparedness System (NPS) which guides activities to enable the nation to achieve the NPG. The NPS allows the nation to track the progress of our ability to build and improve the capabilities necessary to prevent, protect against, mitigate the effects of, respond to, and recover from those threats that pose the greatest risk to the security of the nation. The NPS provides an integrated approach to preparedness that can be implemented and measured at all levels of government. This system is an all-of-nation and whole community approach to preparedness, from neighborhood organizations to civic groups and private businesses. It contains a methodical approach integrated across the preparedness cycle and links together programs and requirements into a comprehensive system, driving rational decision-making and allowing for a direct and defensible assessment of progress against clearly defined objectives. The NPS is based on a consistent methodology for assessing the threats and hazards facing a given jurisdiction. The findings of the assessment drive planning factors and all other components of the preparedness cycle including resource requirements, existing capabilities and capability gaps, driving investments to close those gaps, making and validating improvements in capabilities through training and exercising, and continually assessing progress.
Section 648(b)(1) of the Post-Katrina Emergency Management Reform Act of 2006,
Public Law 109-295
(
6 U.S.C. 748(b)(1)
) also provides for these exercises and states the Administrator “shall carry out a national exercise program to test and evaluate the national preparedness goal, National Incident Management System, National Response, and other related plans and strategies.”
The Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP) provides the program structure, multi-year planning system, tools, and guidance necessary for entities to build and sustain exercise programs that enhance homeland security capabilities, and ultimately, preparedness. The HSEEP After Action Report/Improvement Plan (AAR/IP), Integrated Preparedness Plans (IPPs), and National Exercise Program (NEP) Support Request Form provide standardized methods for reporting the results of exercises, identifying exercise program priorities, and submitting exercise nominations necessary to validate national preparedness capabilities.
This proposed information collection previously published in the
Federal Register
on June 17, 2026, at
91 FR 36605
with a 60-day public comment period. Four public comments were received. FEMA appreciates the commenters' support for maintaining the HSEEP Documentation information collection and recognizes the continued value of HSEEP in supporting consistent exercise design, conduct, evaluation, after-action reporting, improvement planning, grant accountability, and national preparedness analysis. Commenters emphasized that HSEEP templates and documentation help validate preparedness capabilities, support trend analysis, and encourage participation and accountability across components, jurisdictions, and exercise partners. FEMA also acknowledges concerns that current HSEEP templates can be difficult to manipulate, may require duplicative data entry across documents, and can create administrative burden through formatting, reconciliation, and document-management tasks, particularly for smaller or less-resourced exercise programs.
FEMA will consider the recommendations to simplify and modernize HSEEP templates and reduce redundant content across materials, provide clearer minimum documentation guidance for each of the seven exercise types, and support scalable approaches such as simplified forms, digital submission, reusable structured data, conditional fields, and responsible AI use in future revisions of these collection instruments. FEMA notes that Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP doctrine) emphasizes flexibility, scalability, and the appropriate documentation based on exercise purpose and scope.
See
HSEEP doctrine (January 2020), available at
https://preptoolkit.fema.gov/​web/​hseep-resources/​policy-and-guidance
.
FEMA's current collection allows electronic submission, and tools such as the Preparedness Toolkit and Exercise Builder support exercise planning, conduct, evaluation, and documentation. No change to the information collection or the burden estimate is being made during this extension, but FEMA will consider the feedback in future revisions to HSEEP doctrine, templates, forms, supporting tools, and burden analyses. The purpose of this notice is to notify the public that FEMA will submit the information collection abstracted below to the Office
(
printed page 72549)
of Management and Budget for review and clearance.
Collection of Information
Title:
Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP) Documentation.

Extension of a currently approved information collection.

1660-0118.

FEMA Form FF-008-FY-21-102 (formerly 091-0-1), After Action Report/Improvement Plan (AAR/IP); FEMA Form FF-008-FY-21-100 (formerly 008-0-26), Integrated Preparedness Plan (IPP); FEMA Form FF-008-FY-21-101 (formerly 008-0-27), National Exercise Program (NEP) Support Request Form.

The Homeland Security Exercise and Evaluation Program (HSEEP) Documentation collection provides reporting on the results of preparedness exercises and provides assessments of the respondents' capabilities so that strengths and areas for improvement are identified, corrected, and shared as appropriate prior to a real incident. This information is also required to be submitted as part of certain FEMA grant programs.

AGENCY:
U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission.
ACTION:
Notice of open public event.
SUMMARY:
Notice is hereby given of the following open public event of the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission. The Commission is mandated by Congress to monitor,
(
printed page 72632)
investigate, and report to Congress annually on “the national security implications of the bilateral trade and economic relationship between the United States and the People's Republic of China.” Pursuant to this mandate, the Commission will hold a public release of its 2026 Annual Report to Congress in Washington, DC on November 18, 2026.
DATES:
The release is scheduled for Wednesday, November 18, 2026, at 1:00 p.m.
ADDRESSES:
This release will be held in-person at or near the U.S. Capitol and adjacent congressional office buildings (specific building and room number to be announced) and online via live webcast on the Commission's website at
www.uscc.gov
. Please check the Commission's website for an announcement on the specific event location once determined. Instructions on how to view the webcast and submit questions or participate in the question and answer session will also be posted at
USCC.gov.
Reservations are not required to attend.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Any member of the public seeking further information concerning the event should contact Jameson Cunningham, 444 North Capitol Street NW, Suite 602, Washington, DC 20001; telephone: 202-624-1496, or via email at
jcunningham@uscc.gov
.
Reservations are not required to attend.
ADA Accessibility:
For questions about the accessibility of the event or to request an accommodation, please contact Jameson Cunningham at 202-624-1496, or via email at
jcunningham@uscc.gov
.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Topics to Be Discussed: The Commission's 2026 Annual Report to Congress addresses key findings and recommendations for congressional action based upon the Commission's hearings, research, fact-finding travel, and review of areas designated by Congress in its mandate, including focused work this year on: a review of economics, trade, security, and foreign affairs developments in China and in the U.S.-China relationship in 2026; China's relations with India and the future of U.S. strategy in the Indo-Pacific; China's predatory diplomatic practices in Latin America; China's efforts to narrow the United States' advantages in the undersea domain; China's bid to reshape global commodities markets; China's attempts to harness data to advance its economic, technological, intelligence, and military goals; China's bid to control the AI tech stack; and recent developments affecting Taiwan and Hong Kong.
Authority
Congress created the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission in 2000 in the National Defense Authorization Act (
Public Law 106-398
), as amended by Public Laws No. 107-67 (November 12, 2001), No. 108-7 (February 20, 2003), 109-108 (November 22, 2005), No. 110-161 (December 26, 2007), No. 113-291 (December 19, 2014), and No. 117-286 (December 27, 2022).

Title:

OMB Control Number:

Summary of Collection:
The policy of the USDA Forest Service (USDA FS) is stated in Forest Service Handbook (FSH 5109.16, chapters zero code and 20), “Use only evaluated, approved and qualified fire chemicals.” This policy requires the Agency to evaluate all wildland fire chemicals before use in fire management activities on lands managed by the USDA FS. Additionally, the Agency needs “to have available and utilize adequate types and quantities of qualified fire chemical products to accomplish fire management activities safely, efficiently, and effectively.” To accomplish this objective, the USDA FS evaluates fire chemical products available for use in direct wildland-fire management operations prior to such use on lands managed by the Agency. (FSH5109.16, zero code, sections 02 and 03).
Need and Use of the Information:
Information is collected for each formulation or reformulation once, upon the respondent's initial request for evaluation. For the purposes of this information collection, we're anticipating an average of five respondents will submit ten new responses during a twelve-month period. This information collection and the product evaluation must be conducted on an ongoing basis to ensure the Agency can solicit and award contracts in a timely manner to provide firefighters with safe and effective wildland fire chemical products.

(

November 5, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 29, 2026, 24X National Exchange LLC (“24X” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the transaction fees applicable to Members
[
3
]
of the Exchange pursuant to Exchange Rule 15.1(a) and (c). The Exchange proposes to implement the rule change on November 2, 2026. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://equities.24exchange.com/​regulation
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the transaction fees applicable to Members of the Exchange. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to increase the fee for executions of non-retail
[
4
]
and retail
[
5
]
orders that remove liquidity from the 24X Book
[
6
]
in all securities traded on the Exchange priced below $1.00 per share (“Removed Sub-Dollar Volume”) from 0.09% of the total dollar value of the transaction to 0.28% of the total dollar value of the transaction. The Exchange proposes to implement the rule change on November 2, 2026.
The proposed increased fee for Removed Sub-Dollar Volume transactions are consistent with or lower than the fees charged by other exchanges for similar executions,
[
7
]
and are intended to incentivize Members to increase the liquidity-providing orders they submit to the Exchange, which would support price discovery on the Exchange and provide additional liquidity for incoming orders.
The proposed rule change does not include different fees depending on the number of orders submitted to, or transactions executed on or through, the Exchange. Accordingly, the fees described above are applicable to all Members, regardless of the overall volume of a Member's trading activities on the Exchange.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b)
[
8
]
of the Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(4)
[
9
]
of the Act in particular, in that it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities. Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed amended fees are consistent with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5)
[
10
]
of the Act in that they are designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and, particularly, are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes that the proposed amended fees reflect a simple and competitive pricing structure designed to incentivize market participants to add aggressively priced displayed liquidity and direct their order flow to the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would promote price discovery and price formation and deepen liquidity that is subject to the Exchange's transparency, regulation, and oversight as an exchange, thereby enhancing market quality to the benefit of all Members and investors.
The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and self-regulatory organization revenues, and also recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
11
]
As illustrated in the following table, the Exchange notes that the proposed amended fees are comparable to or lower than those in place on other exchanges:
(
printed page 72589)
Exchange
Fee for removed volume
                             <$1.00 (non-retail)
Fee for removed volume
                             <$1.00 (retail)
24X

0.28% of total dollar value.
Cboe EDGX

0.30% of total dollar value.
MIAX Pearl

The Exchange believes that it is appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act to charge a fee of 0.28% of the total dollar value of Removed Sub-Dollar Volume non-retail and retail transactions because it is comparable to or lower than the fees charged by other exchanges for similar transactions.
[
12
]
The Exchange further believes that this fee is equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory because it applies equally to all Members, and is designed to facilitate increased activity on the Exchange to the benefit of all Members by providing more trading opportunities and promoting price discovery.
In conclusion, the Exchange submits that its proposed amended fee structure satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4)
[
13
]
and 6(b)(5)
[
14
]
of the Act for the reasons discussed above in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities, does not permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers, and is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and in general to protect investors and the public interest, particularly as the proposal neither targets nor will it have a disparate impact on any particular category of market participant. As described more fully below in the Exchange's statement regarding the burden on competition, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces, and believes that its proposed amended fee structure is an appropriate effort to address such forces.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as discussed above, the Exchange believes that the proposed changes would encourage the submission of order flow to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, execution incentives, and enhanced execution opportunities, as well as price discovery and transparency for all Members. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed changes further the Commission's goal in adopting Regulation NMS of fostering competition among orders, which promotes “more efficient pricing of individual stocks for all types of orders, large and small.”
[
15
]
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. To the contrary, the Exchange believes that the proposed amended pricing structure will increase competition and is intended to draw volume to the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or reduce use of certain categories of products in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees and rebates, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. As a new exchange, the Exchange faces intense competition from existing exchanges and other non-exchange venues that provide markets for equities trading.
Although these pricing incentives are intended to attract liquidity to the Exchange, most other exchanges in operation today already offer multiple incentives to their participants, including tiered pricing that provides higher rebates or discounted executions, and other exchanges will be able to modify such incentives in order to compete with the Exchange. As discussed above, the Exchange notes that the proposed amended fees are comparable to or lower than those in place on other exchanges. Accordingly, with respect to a market participant deciding to submit an order to remove liquidity, there are multiple exchanges that will continue to be competitively priced for such orders when compared to the Exchange's pricing. Further, while pricing incentives do cause shifts of liquidity between trading centers, market participants make determinations on where to provide liquidity or route orders to take liquidity based on factors other than pricing, including technology, functionality, and other considerations. Consequently, the Exchange believes that the degree to which its proposed amended fees could impose any burden on competition is extremely limited, and does not believe that such pricing structure would burden competition of Members or competing venues in a manner that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed amended fees apply equally to all Members. The proposed pricing structure is intended to encourage market participants to add liquidity on the Exchange by charging fees that are comparable to or lower than those offered by other exchanges, which the Exchange believes will help to encourage Members to send orders to the Exchange to the benefit of all Exchange participants. As the proposed rates are equally applicable to all Members, regardless of the overall volume of a Member's trading activities on the Exchange, the Exchange does not believe there is any burden on intramarket competition.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
16
]
of the Act and
(
printed page 72590)
subparagraph (f)(2) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
17
]
because it establishes a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the Exchange. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
18
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-24X-2026-29 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-29. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-24X-2026-29 and should be submitted on or before December 1, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
19
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106834; File No. SR-FICC-2026-008]
November 5, 2026.
I. Introduction
On July 24, 2026, Fixed Income Clearing Corporation (“FICC”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change SR-FICC-2026-008 pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4
[
2
]
thereunder to modify FICC's Government Securities Division (“GSD”) Rulebook (“GSD Rules”)
[
3
]
to establish a guaranty fund designed to cover losses that may arise due to a Member default or non-default loss event.
[
4
]
On August 4, 2026, FICC filed Partial Amendment No. 1 to make clarifications and corrections to the proposed rule change (the proposed rule change, as modified by Partial Amendment No. 1, is hereinafter referred to as the “Proposed Rule Change”).
[
5
]
The Proposed Rule Change was published for public comment in the
Federal Register
on August 11, 2026.
[
6
]
The Commission has received
(
printed page 72593)
comments regarding the substance of the changes proposed in the Proposed Rule Change.
[
7
]
On September 15, 2026, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Exchange Act,
[
8
]
the Commission designated a longer period within which to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove the Proposed Rule Change.
[
9
]
The Commission is instituting proceedings, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Exchange Act,
[
10
]
to determine whether to approve or disapprove the Proposed Rule Change.
II. Summary of the Proposed Rule Change
A. Background
FICC, through GSD, serves as a central counterparty (“CCP”) and provider of clearance and settlement services for transactions in U.S. government securities, including repurchase and reverse repurchase transactions involving U.S. government securities.
[
11
]
FICC manages its credit exposures to its Netting Members through the collection of margin to mitigate potential losses from arising from a Member default. FICC maintains financial resources in the form of its Clearing Fund, which is designed to enable FICC to cover potential losses resulting from the failure of the Member or Member family to which FICC has the largest credit exposure. FICC collects Clearing Fund deposits (
i.e.,
Required Fund Deposits) from its Members using a risk-based margin methodology. Required Fund Deposits operate, individually, as each Member's initial margin, and the aggregate of all such Members' deposits is referred to collectively as the Clearing Fund, which currently operates as GSD's default fund. FICC states that this risk-based methodology enables FICC to identify the risks posed by a Member's unsettled portfolio and to quickly adjust and collect additional deposits as needed to cover those risks.
[
12
]
B. Proposed Rule Change
FICC proposes to establish a Guaranty Fund for GSD, designed to cover losses that may arise due to a Member default or a non-default loss event and enable FICC to support bankruptcy remote treatment for its Clearing Fund deposits. The Proposed Rule Change includes, among other things:
Adopting new GSD Rule 4A (Guaranty Fund) to set forth requirements for the Guaranty Fund, including, among other things, that: (i) FICC performs daily stress testing using historical and hypothetical scenarios for purposes of sizing the Guaranty Fund; (ii) FICC sizes the Guaranty Fund at an amount sufficient to cover the stress test deficiency (
i.e.,
losses observed in daily stress testing over required Clearing Fund deposits) that may arise as a result of the default of the two Netting Member Affiliated Families
[
13
]
that would potentially cause the largest aggregate credit exposure for FICC in extreme but plausible market conditions (a “Cover 2 Standard” or “Cover 2 Requirement”); (iii) all deposits to the Guaranty Fund must be made in cash; and (iv) FICC has the authority to resize the Guaranty Fund on an intramonth basis if stress test deficiencies breach certain thresholds.
Modifying GSD Rule 4 and the Margin Component Schedule to: (i) support bankruptcy remote treatment for Clearing Fund deposits; (ii) exclude the Clearing Fund from loss mutualization; (iii) provide FICC with the authority to require additional margin deposits from Netting Members if their stress test deficiencies exceed predetermined thresholds in relation to the total Required Fund Deposits of all other Members (excluding such Member or Affiliated Family) or would cause the Guaranty Fund to exceed upper bound parameters established for limiting the resizing of the Guaranty Fund; (iv) clarify that FICC would no longer have the authority to “borrow” Clearing Fund deposits of non-defaulting Members to provide liquidity to FICC to meet its settlement obligations; (v) provide FICC with the authority to exchange a Netting Member's Clearing Fund deposit in the form of cash for U.S. Treasury securities to provide liquidity to FICC to meet its settlement obligations; and (vi) eliminate fixed minimum Required Fund Deposit amounts and adjust the associated minimum cash composition requirements accordingly.
Relocating the loss allocation rules in Section 7 of GSD Rule 4 to a new GSD Rule 4C (Loss Allocation) and modifying the rules to: (i) incorporate the proposed Guaranty Fund into the loss allocation rules and exclude the Clearing Fund from loss mutualization; (ii) eliminate the concept of Tier One Netting Members and Tier Two Members and exclude CCIT Members and Registered Investment Company Netting Members from loss allocation; (iii) adopt a new five-day “cooling off period” for Defaulting Member Events and Declared Non-Default Loss Events (also referred to as an “Event Period”); and (iv) impose an assessment cap on loss allocation during each cooling-off period equal to two times (or 200 percent of) the Member's Guaranty Fund requirement for each Event Period in lieu of the existing loss allocation rounds system.
Make other conforming changes throughout the GSD Rules to reflect the adoption of the Guaranty Fund, as described more fully in the Notice of Filing.
[
14
]
III. Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove the Proposed Rule Change and Grounds for Disapproval Under Consideration
The Commission is instituting proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Exchange Act to determine whether the Proposed Rule Change should be approved or disapproved.
[
15
]
Institution of proceedings is appropriate at this time in view of the legal and policy issues raised by the Proposed Rule Change. Institution of proceedings does not indicate that the Commission has reached any conclusions with respect to any of the issues involved. Rather, the Commission seeks and encourages interested persons to comment on the Proposed Rule Change, which would provide the Commission with arguments to support the Commission's analysis as to whether to approve or disapprove the Proposed Rule Change.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Exchange Act,
[
16
]
the Commission is providing notice of the grounds for disapproval under consideration. The Commission is instituting proceedings
(
printed page 72594)
to allow for additional analysis of, and input from commenters with respect to, the Proposed Rule Change's consistency with Section 17A of the Exchange Act
[
17
]
and the rules thereunder, including the following provisions:
Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Exchange Act,
[
18
]
which requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency are designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions; to assure the safeguarding of securities and funds which are in the custody or control of the clearing agency or for which it is responsible; and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest;
Section 17A(b)(3)(I) of the Exchange Act,
[
19
]
which requires that the rules of a clearing agency do not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act;
Rule 17ad-22(e)(4) under the Exchange Act,
[
20
]
which requires that a covered clearing agency establish, implement, maintain, and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to effectively identify, measure, monitor, and manage its credit exposures to participants and those arising from its payment, clearing, and settlement processes;
Rule 17ad-22(e)(6)(iii) under the Exchange Act,
[
21
]
which requires that a covered clearing agency establish written policies and procedures reasonably designed to cover its credit exposures to its participants by establishing a risk-based margin system that, at a minimum, calculates margin sufficient to cover its potential future exposure to participants in the interval between the last margin collection and the close out of positions following a participant default;
Rule 17ad-22(e)(7)(i) under the Exchange Act,
[
22
]
which requires that a covered clearing agency effectively measure, monitor, and manage the liquidity risk that arises in or is borne by the covered clearing agency, including measuring, monitoring, and managing its settlement and funding flows on an ongoing and timely basis, and its use of intraday liquidity by, at a minimum, maintaining sufficient liquid resources at the minimum in all relevant currencies to effect same-day and, where appropriate, intraday and multiday settlement of payment obligations with a high degree of confidence under a wide range of foreseeable stress scenarios that includes, but is not limited to, the default of the participant family that would generate the largest aggregate payment obligation for the covered clearing agency in extreme but plausible market conditions;
Rule 17ad-22(e)(7)(ix) under the Exchange Act,
[
23
]
which requires that a covered clearing agency establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to describe its process to replenish any liquid resources that it may employ during a stress event;
Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(i) under the Exchange Act,
[
24
]
which requires that a covered clearing agency establish, implement, maintain, and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to establish objective, risk-based, and publicly disclosed criteria for participation, which, permit fair and open access by direct, and where relevant, indirect participants and other financial market utilities;
Rule 17Ad-22(e)(23) under the Exchange Act,

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106833; File No. SR-ICC-2026-014]
(
printed page 72601)
November 5, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Securities Exchange Act” or the “Act”),
15 U.S.C. 78s(b)(1)
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
17 CFR 240.19b-4
, notice is hereby given that on November 02, 2026, ICE Clear Credit LLC (“ICC” or “ICE Clear Credit”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or the “Commission”) the proposed rule change, as described in Items I, II and III below, which Items have been prepared primarily by ICC. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The principal purpose of the proposed rule change is to adopt the ICC Procedures for Monitoring Compliance with the Eligible Secondary Market Transaction Submission Requirements (the “ESMT Procedures”). The ESMT Procedures supplement existing provisions of the ICC U.S. Treasury (“UST” or “Treasury”) Clearing Rules
[
1
]
(the “Treasury Rules”).
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, ICC included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change, security-based swap submission, or advance notice and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change, security-based swap submission, or advance notice. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. ICC has prepared summaries, set forth in sections (A), (B), and (C) below, of the most significant aspects of these statements.
(A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
(a) Purpose
ICC proposes to adopt the ESMT Procedures, which formalize ICC's procedures for monitoring compliance by Treasury Participants (“TPs”) with the requirement to submit Eligible Secondary Market Transactions
[
2
]
for clearing, consistent with Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or the “Commission”) Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(A) and (B).
[
3
]
The ESMT Procedures supplement existing provisions of the Treasury Rules, including Chapter 2—Membership, Chapter 3—Clearing of Contracts and Chapter 7—Disciplinary Rules. The ESMT Procedures establish how ICC will monitor, review and enforce TP compliance with Treasury Rule 303. ICC intends to adopt these ESMT Procedures to support the clearing of UST securities through its new Treasury clearing service.
[
4
]
ICC proposes to make such changes effective following Commission approval of the proposed rule change.
The ESMT Procedures consist of three sections. Section 1 specifies that capitalized terms used but not defined in the ESMT Procedures have the meanings specified in the Treasury Rules, unless otherwise indicated.
Section 2 sets out the requirement to submit trades for clearing. As specified in Section 2.1, Treasury Rule 303 requires each TP to submit to ICC or another SEC-registered covered clearing agency for clearing, promptly after execution, all trades in contracts that are eligible for clearing at ICC and are Eligible Secondary Market Transactions to which it is a counterparty. ICC will publish on its website all trades in contracts that are eligible for clearing at ICC pursuant to Chapter 30 of the Treasury Rules. A TP may satisfy this requirement by submitting the trade to ICC or to another SEC-registered covered clearing agency. ICC believes the ESMT Procedures that describe how compliance will be monitored provide TPs with transparency and give ICC a clear, documented process for carrying out its monitoring responsibility.
Pursuant to Section 2.2, the ESMT Procedures require TPs to promptly notify ICC in writing within 30 calendar days from the date on which the TP learns that it is no longer in compliance with Treasury Rule 303. The notice must include all relevant facts known at the time, such as the approximate duration of the non-compliance, the time at which the non-compliance was remediated or the anticipated remediation steps and expected timing, and the name and contact information of the TP staff member overseeing the matter.
In addition, Section 2.2 of the ESMT Procedures require each TP to annually attest to compliance with Treasury Rule 303 (“Annual Attestation”). ICC will announce the due date to TPs, with the due date being no less than 30 calendar days after the announcement. A senior officer authorized to sign for the TP must sign the Annual Attestation and confirm the TP has effective controls in place to ensure compliance with Treasury Rule 303. In the Annual Attestation, the attesting officer must state that they have read and understand the trade submission requirements set forth in the Treasury Rules and in the ESMT Procedures. The attesting officer must also state that the TP has established, maintains and enforces policies, procedures or other controls reasonably designed to ensure ongoing compliance with Treasury Rule 303, and that those controls are reasonably designed to promptly identify and remediate any non-compliance. Finally, the attesting officer must state that the TP complied with Treasury Rule 303 during the 12 months before the date of the attestation.
In Section 2.2, the ESMT Procedures further reserve ICC's right to conduct periodic reviews of a TP's submission of trades that are eligible for clearing and are Eligible Secondary Market Transactions. These reviews may cover transactions submitted to ICC as well as submissions to other covered clearing agencies, including rejected submissions and attempts to re-submit transactions. ICC may ask a TP for information and supporting documentation showing how it resolved any rejections or re-submissions in order to comply with Treasury Rule 303. ICC may also ask for information about
(
printed page 72602)
timeliness of submission for clearing following execution of the transaction.
Finally, the ESMT Procedures describe how ICC will address possible violations of Treasury Rule 303 in Section 3. Under its authority in Treasury Rule 701(a), ICC may initiate and conduct investigations into alleged violations of a TP's obligation to comply with Treasury Rule 303, and ICC staff will conduct those investigations in accordance with Treasury Rule 702. If ICC staff believes a violation may have occurred, staff will consider a non-exclusive list of mitigating factors when exercising discretion to issue a warning letter, to negotiate the terms of a written settlement agreement (including the amount of fines) or to make penalty recommendations to the ICC Business Conduct Committee or Review Subcommittee of the Business Conduct Committee.
[
5
]
Those factors include whether the TP self-reported the non-compliance, any history of the TP violating Treasury Rule 303, remediation efforts by the TP, the extent of the TP's cooperation with an ICC investigation, whether the possible violation involved single or multiple transactions, and the period over which any multiple violations occurred.
(b) Statutory Basis
ICC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Section 17A of the Act
[
6
]
and the regulations thereunder applicable to it, including the applicable standards under Rule 17ad-22.
[
7
]
In particular, Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act
[
8
]
requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, to assure the safeguarding of securities and funds in the custody or control of ICC or for which it is responsible, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. As described above, the proposed ESMT Procedures are designed to support the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act,
[
9
]
by supporting TP compliance with the Eligible Secondary Market Transaction submission requirements. As described above, ICC believes the ESMT Procedures that describe how compliance will be monitored provide TPs with transparency and give ICC a clear, documented process for carrying out its monitoring responsibility. ICC further believes that having written policies and procedures that clearly document how it will monitor compliance with the Eligible Secondary Market Transaction submission requirements supports the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, and protects investors and the public interest, consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.
[
10
]
In addition, Section 17A(b)(3)(G) of the Act
[
11
]
requires that the rules of the clearing agency provide that its participants shall be appropriately disciplined for violation of any provision of the rules of the clearing agency, including by fine or other fitting sanction. The proposed changes are designed to ensure that TPs are appropriately disciplined for violations of Treasury Rule 303. As described above, under its authority in Treasury Rule 701(a), ICC may initiate and conduct investigations into alleged violations of a TP's obligation to comply with Treasury Rule 303, and ICC staff will conduct those investigations in accordance with Treasury Rule 702. If ICC staff believes a violation may have occurred, staff will consider a non-exclusive list of mitigating factors when exercising discretion to issue a warning letter, to negotiate the terms of a written settlement agreement (including the amount of fines) or to make recommendations to the ICC Business Conduct Committee or Review Subcommittee of the Business Conduct Committee.
[
12
]
The proposed ESMT Procedures are thus consistent with the requirements of Section 17A(b)(3)(G) of the Act.
[
13
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(A)
[
14
]
requires a covered clearing agency that provides central counterparty services for U.S. Treasury securities to establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to have objective, risk-based and publicly disclosed criteria for participation that require each direct participant to submit for clearance and settlement all eligible secondary market transactions to which it is a counterparty. As described above, the proposed ESMT Procedures require each TP to submit to ICC (or another SEC registered covered clearing agency) for clearing all trades in contracts that are eligible for clearing at ICC and are Eligible Secondary Market Transactions to which it is a counterparty, consistent with Treasury Rule 303, and to confirm annually that it has complied with that requirement and maintains policies, procedures, or controls reasonably designed to ensure continued compliance. ICC therefore believes the proposed ESMT Procedures are consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(A).
[
15
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(B)
[
16
]
requires a covered clearing agency that provides central counterparty services for U.S. Treasury securities to establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to identify and monitor its direct participants' submission of those transactions for clearing, including how the covered clearing agency would address a failure to submit transactions in accordance with the relevant requirements. As described above, the proposed ESMT Procedures establish how ICC will identify and monitor TP compliance with Treasury Rule 303. Under the proposed ESMT Procedures, TPs must notify ICC in writing within 30 calendar days of learning that it is no longer in compliance, TPs must provide an Annual Attestation signed by a senior officer, and ICC may conduct periodic reviews of TP submissions, including rejected submissions, re-submissions and timeliness of submission following execution. The proposed ESMT Procedures also describe how ICC will address a failure to submit transactions in accordance with Treasury Rule 303. ICC may investigate possible violations pursuant to Treasury Rules 701(a) and 702, and ICC staff will consider identified mitigating factors in determining whether to issue a warning letter, negotiate a written settlement agreement or make penalty recommendations. ICC therefore believes the proposed ESMT Procedures are consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(18)(iv)(B).
[
17
]
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
ICC does not believe the proposed rule change will have any impact, or impose any burden, on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance
(
printed page 72603)
of the purposes of the Act. The proposed ESMT Procedures will apply uniformly across all market participants. ICC does not believe the proposed rule change would adversely affect the costs of clearing or the ability of market participants to access clearing. Therefore, ICC does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is inappropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants or Others
Written comments relating to the proposed rule change have not been solicited received. ICC will notify the Commission of any written comments received by ICC.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Within 45 days of the date of publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
or within such longer period up to 90 days (i) as the Commission may designate if it finds such longer period to be appropriate and publishes its reasons for so finding or (ii) as to which the self-regulatory organization consents, the Commission will:
(A) by order approve or disapprove such proposed rule change, or
(B) institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be disapproved.
(IV) Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File Number SR-ICC-2026-014 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-ICC-2026-014. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of such filings will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of ICE Clear Credit and on ICE Clear Credit's website at
https://www.ice.com/​clear-credit/​regulation
.
Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-ICC-2026-014 and should be submitted on or before December 1, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
18
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.
